places.name: Conwy Castle
places.ai_summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, this 13th-century fortress was built by Edward I. It features eight massive towers and offers stunning views of the Conwy estuary.

opening_hours.notes: Hours vary seasonally; check website before visiting.

places.place_tip: Climb the towers for panoramic views of the town and estuary.
places.address: Rose Hill St, Conwy LL32 8AY, United Kingdom

places.name: Conwy Town Walls
places.ai_summary: A well-preserved medieval wall encircling the historic town of Conwy. Visitors can walk along the walls for unique views of the castle and harbor.

opening_hours.notes: Accessible via various entry points around the town.

places.place_tip: Start your walk at the Upper Gate for the best views of the castle.

places.name: The Smallest House in Great Britain
places.ai_summary: A quirky tourist attraction, this tiny red house measures just 72 inches wide and 122 inches high. It was last inhabited in 1900 and offers a glimpse into minimalist living.
places.name_english: The Smallest House in Great Britain
places.place_tip: Take a photo outside the house for a fun souvenir.
places.address: Conwy Quay, Conwy LL32 8BB, United Kingdom

places.name: Conwy Quay & Mussel Boats
places.ai_summary: A picturesque quay with colorful mussel boats. It's a great spot for a leisurely stroll and offers boat trips on the Conwy Estuary.
places.place_tip: Enjoy a boat trip for a unique view of the town and castle.
places.address: Conwy Quay, Conwy LL32 8BB, United Kingdom

places.ai_summary: An exquisite example of Elizabethan architecture, Plas Mawr is a restored town house with period furnishings and beautiful gardens.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays; check website for seasonal variations.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the stunning plasterwork and the beautiful garden.

places.name: Conwy Suspension Bridge
places.ai_summary: An iconic symbol of Conwy, this suspension bridge was designed by Thomas Telford and completed in 1826. It offers stunning views of the Conwy Castle and the estuary.

opening_hours.notes: Best viewed at sunrise or sunset.

places.place_tip: Walk across the bridge for breathtaking views and great photo opportunities.

places.name: Bodnant Garden
places.ai_summary: A stunning 80-acre garden renowned for its horticultural excellence, featuring a wide variety of plants, trees, and shrubs, as well as beautiful views of the Conwy Estuary.

opening_hours.notes: Last entry one hour before closing; check website for seasonal variations.

places.place_tip: Visit the Dell for a peaceful retreat and great views.
places.address: Bodnant Rd, Tal-y-Cafn, Colwyn Bay LL28 5RE, United Kingdom

places.name: Aberconwy House (NT)
places.ai_summary: A medieval merchant's house, now a National Trust property, showcasing period furnishings and offering insights into medieval life in Wales.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays; check website for seasonal variations.

places.place_tip: Join a guided tour to learn more about the history of the house and its inhabitants.

places.name: St Mary’s Church Conwy
places.ai_summary: A historic church dating back to the 12th century, known for its beautiful stained glass windows and impressive tower.

opening_hours.notes: Check website for service times and seasonal variations.

places.place_tip: Attend a service or concert for a unique experience.

places.name: Marine Walk
places.ai_summary: A scenic coastal walk offering stunning views of the Conwy Estuary, the Great Orme, and the Snowdonia mountains.
places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes and bring a camera for the stunning views.

places.name: RSPB Conwy Nature Reserve
places.ai_summary: A beautiful nature reserve managed by the RSPB, featuring a variety of habitats and a wide range of bird species. Ideal for nature walks and birdwatching.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Christmas Day; check website for seasonal variations.

places.place_tip: Visit the hides for the best birdwatching opportunities.

places.ai_summary: A popular day trip destination, the Great Orme is a limestone headland with stunning coastal views, a historic copper mine, and a scenic tramway.

places.place_tip: Take the tramway to the summit for spectacular views.

places.ai_summary: A challenging walk to the summit of Tal y Fan, offering breathtaking views of Snowdonia and the North Wales coast.
